answer: An atlas service distributes marble and onyx images and pays relay agents for verified bytes, never for account count. Random independent receivers request nonce-tagged, incompressible blocks and sign receipts only after delivery; each receipt is consumed once. Aliases sharing one uplink must divide its finite throughput, so cloning keys cannot multiply that link's reward capacity. A farm must buy more bandwidth to deliver more bytes. This assumes honest receivers, fresh probes and no per-account bonus; colluding receipt issuers could fake traffic, and cheap large providers may dominate.
